solution: A logarithm's base must be positive and not equal to 1. So for \(\log_a x\) to be defined, \(a\) must be any positive real number \(\neq 1\).
If \(\log_2 7 = \dfrac{p}{q}\) were rational, then \(2^p = 7^q\) — impossible (LHS even, RHS odd). So \(\log_2 7\) is irrational (hence neither integer nor prime).
\(\log\dfrac{a+b}{2} = \dfrac12(\log a + \log b) = \log\sqrt{ab}\) gives \(\dfrac{a+b}{2} = \sqrt{ab}\), i.e. A.M. = G.M., so \(a = b\).

For \(\alpha > 1\), \(\log_b \alpha = \dfrac{\ln\alpha}{\ln b}\) decreases as the base \(b\) increases. Since \(10 > 3 > e > 2\), increasing order is \(\log_{10}\alpha, \log_3\alpha, \log_e\alpha, \log_2\alpha\).

\(\log ab\) is defined only when \(ab > 0\), so \(a\) and \(b\) are non-zero and have the same sign. Then \(\log ab - \log|b| = \log\dfrac{ab}{|b|}\). If \(b > 0\) then \(|b| = b\), so \(\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = a\), and here \(a > 0\), giving \(a = |a|\). If \(b < 0\) then \(|b| = -b\), so \(\dfrac{ab}{|b|} = -a\), and here \(a < 0\), giving \(-a = |a|\). Either way the quotient is \(|a|\), so the expression equals \(\log|a|\). The alternative \(\log a\) is not valid in general: when \(a\) and \(b\) are both negative it is undefined, while \(\log|a|\) holds throughout the domain. Hence (B).
By change of base the product telescopes: \(\log_3 4 \cdot \log_4 5 \cdots \log_8 9 = \log_3 9 = \log_3 3^2 = 2\).

The expression \(= \log\left[\left(\dfrac{16}{15}\right)^7\left(\dfrac{25}{24}\right)^5\left(\dfrac{81}{80}\right)^3\right]\). The exponents of 3 and 5 cancel (\(0\) each) and 2 has exponent \(28 - 15 - 12 = 1\), so it equals \(\log 2\).

\(\log_4 5 = a \Rightarrow \log 5 = 2a\log 2\); \(\log_5 6 = b \Rightarrow \log 6 = 2ab\log 2\). But \(\log 6 = \log 2 + \log 3\), so \(\log 3 = (2ab - 1)\log 2\), giving \(\log_3 2 = \dfrac{1}{2ab - 1}\).
\(\log_k x \cdot \log_5 k = \log_5 x\) (change of base), so \(\log_5 x = \log_x 5 = \dfrac{1}{\log_5 x}\), giving \((\log_5 x)^2 = 1\), i.e. \(\log_5 x = \pm 1\). Hence \(x = 5\) or \(x = \dfrac15\).
\(\log_5 a \cdot \log_a x = \log_5 x = 2\), so \(x = 5^2 = 25\).
\((a + 2b)^2 = a^2 + 4b^2 + 4ab = 12ab + 4ab = 16ab\). Taking logs: \(2\log(a + 2b) = \log 16 + \log a + \log b\), so \(\log(a + 2b) = \dfrac12[\log a + \log b + 4\log 2]\).
\(1 + x = \log_a(abc)\), so \((1 + x)^{-1} = \log_{abc} a\); similarly for \(y, z\). Their sum is \(\log_{abc}(abc) = 1\).

Change of base gives the chain rule \(\log_x y \cdot \log_z x = \log_z y\). So \(bc = \log_{36}24 \cdot \log_{48}36 = \log_{48}24\), and hence \(abc = a\,(bc) = \log_{24}12 \cdot \log_{48}24 = \log_{48}12\). Therefore \(1 + abc = \log_{48}48 + \log_{48}12 = \log_{48}(48 \cdot 12) = \log_{48}576 = \log_{48}\left(24^{2}\right) = 2\log_{48}24 = 2bc\). Hence (C).
\(a^x = b, b^y = c, c^z = a\) give \(x = \log_a b\), \(y = \log_b c\), \(z = \log_c a\), so \(xyz = \log_a a = 1\).
\(\dfrac{1}{\log_{2^n} a} = \log_a 2^n = n\log_a 2\). So the sum \(= \log_a 2 \sum_{n=1}^{n} n = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\log_a 2\).

\(\log_7\log_5\left(\sqrt{x^2 + x + 5}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow \log_5\left(\sqrt{x^2 + x + 5}\right) = 1 \Rightarrow \sqrt{x^2 + x + 5} = 5 \Rightarrow x^2 + x + 5 = 25 \Rightarrow x^2 + x - 20 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 4)(x + 5) = 0\), so \(x = 4\) or \(x = -5\). Both are genuine roots: at \(x = -5\) we get \(x^2 + x + 5 = 25\), \(\sqrt{25} = 5\), \(\log_5 5 = 1\) and \(\log_7 1 = 0\), with every logarithm defined. So the equation has solution set \(\{4,\ -5\}\); of these only \(x = 4\) is offered among the alternatives, so that is the one to mark. Hence (C).

\(\log_4 18 = \dfrac{\log_2 18}{\log_2 4} = \dfrac{\log_2 18}{2} = \dfrac{1 + \log_2 9}{2}\). Now \(\log_2 9\) is irrational: it is positive, so if it were rational we could write \(\log_2 9 = p/q\) with \(p, q\) positive integers, giving \(2^{p} = 9^{q}\) - impossible, since the left side is even and the right side is odd. Finally, if \(\dfrac{1 + \log_2 9}{2}\) were rational then \(\log_2 9\) would be rational as well, so the whole expression is irrational. Hence (B).
